Life support machines are medical devices that replace or assist failing vital organs. Common types include mechanical ventilators for breathing, ECMO machines for combined heart-lung bypass, dialysis machines for kidney failure, ventricular assist devices for heart pumping, and defibrillators to restore heart rhythm. [](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/treatments/12362-life-support-measures)

- **Mechanical Ventilator:** Pumps oxygen into the lungs and removes carbon dioxide through a tube in the airway.

- **ECMO (Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation):** Pumps blood outside the body through an artificial lung to oxygenate it when lungs and heart are too sick. [](https://www.orlandohealth.com/content-hub/what-does-it-mean-to-be-on-life-support)

### Heart and Circulation

- **VAD (Ventricular Assist Device):**

Helps a weak heart pump blood to the rest of the body.

- **Defibrillator / AED:** Delivers an electric shock to fix dangerous heart rhythms.

- **Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump (IABP):** A balloon device placed in the aorta to help blood flow out of the heart. [](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/treatments/12362-life-support-measures)

### Kidneys and Waste

- **Dialysis Machine:** Cleans toxins, extra salt, and water from the blood when kidneys fail. [](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/treatments/12362-life-support-measures)
